description: DEF CON 27 Main Stage — 90 talks from the canonical 2019 playlist covering offensive security, cloud attacks, wireless exploitation, hardware hacking, privacy, policy, and hacker culture from Las Vegas.

talks.title: Panel: DEF CON to Help Hackers Anonymously Submit Bugs to the Government
talks.teaser: DEF CON launches a structured program for hackers to anonymously report vulnerabilities to US federal agencies.
talks.summary:
DEF CON Hacker-to-Government Vulnerability Disclosure

Jeff Moss (The Dark Tangent) chairs a panel with Katie Moussouris (founder of Luta Security, architect of the first bug bounty programs at Microsoft and HackerOne) and Harley Geiger (Director of Public Policy, Rapid7) to announce a new DEF CON initiative to bridge the gap between the hacker community and US federal agencies on vulnerability disclosure.

The Problem: Lack of Safe Harbors

The panel outlines how security researchers remain reluctant to report vulnerabilities in government systems due to fears of prosecution under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA). Federal civilian agencies have no public vulnerability disclosure policies (VDPs), leaving hackers with no clear path to report issues without legal risk.

DEF CON's Role as Intermediary

DEF CON proposes acting as a trusted third party to receive researcher reports, strip identifying information, and pass validated findings to relevant agencies. This model draws on precedents from coordinated disclosure in the private sector.

Progress and Policy Outlook

The Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 20-01 is discussed as a near-term policy vehicle. Panelists urge CISA and OMB to mandate VDPs across all civilian agencies, creating clear safe harbor language so that good-faith research is protected.

talks.title: Joe Grand - Behind the Scenes of the DEF CON 27 Badge
talks.teaser: Joe Grand reveals the engineering, puzzle design, and Easter eggs embedded in the DC27 hardware badge.
talks.summary:
The DC27 Badge: Engineering the Annual Puzzle

Joe Grand (Kingpin), hardware engineer and DEF CON badge designer, walks through the full lifecycle of creating the DEF CON 27 official conference badge — from concept to production.

Design Philosophy and Puzzle Architecture

Grand discusses how each year's badge must deliver a self-contained puzzle experience without external infrastructure. The DC27 badge used a custom PCB with an FPGA-based processor, LED matrix, and cryptographic challenge layers deliberately seeded with red herrings.

Engineering Challenges

Grand reveals supply chain headaches including last-minute component substitutions, factory errors in board revision management, and the challenge of shipping thousands of working badges with tight power budgets.

Easter Eggs and Solve Path

The talk covers hidden clues, intentional misdirection, and the community collaboration model that DEF CON leverages annually — where hundreds of hackers work collaboratively online to solve the badge challenge within hours of the conference opening.

talks.title: Cult of the Dead Cow - Change the World, cDc Style
talks.teaser: cDc members, including presidential candidate Beto O'Rourke, discuss the group's 35 years of hacktivism and political impact.
talks.summary:
Cult of the Dead Cow: Three Decades of Hacktivism

The Cult of the Dead Cow (cDc), one of the oldest and most influential hacker groups in history, convenes on the DEF CON stage to discuss how they've shaped both hacker culture and political discourse over 35+ years.

Beto O'Rourke's Revelation

The panel includes former Texas congressman and 2020 presidential candidate Beto O'Rourke, whose membership in cDc (under the handle 'Psychedelic Warlord') is publicly acknowledged for the first time in Joseph Menn's book 'Cult of the Dead Cow: How the Original Hacking Supergroup Might Just Save the World.' O'Rourke discusses how his early hacking experiences shaped his views on privacy, government overreach, and technology policy.

Legacy and Impact

cDc members recount founding Back Orifice (the first major remote administration tool that exposed Windows security failures), pioneering hacktivism campaigns targeting authoritarian governments, and launching the Hacktivismo project to develop privacy and circumvention tools for oppressed populations.

Hacker Ethos Meets Politics

The panel reflects on the tension between the hacker community's skepticism of authority and the practical realities of running for office, engaging with government, and advocating for digital rights within existing power structures.

talks.title: Andreas Baumhof - Are Quantum Computers Really A Threat To Cryptography?
talks.teaser: Separates hype from reality on quantum computing's timeline for breaking current public-key cryptography.
talks.summary:
Quantum Threat to Cryptography: Reality Check

Andreas Baumhof, CTO at QuSecure, presents a rigorous technical and timeline-based assessment of whether quantum computers pose a credible near-term threat to RSA, ECC, and other asymmetric cryptosystems.

Shor's Algorithm and the RSA Threat

The talk explains Shor's algorithm's theoretical ability to factor large integers in polynomial time on a fault-tolerant quantum computer. Current quantum hardware requires millions of physical qubits with low error rates to break 2048-bit RSA, far beyond today's ~50-qubit NISQ devices.

Timeline Analysis

Baumhof provides a structured timeline review: realistic projections place cryptographically relevant quantum computers 10–15+ years away, but the 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat model means adversaries may already be capturing encrypted traffic for future decryption.

Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration

The talk advocates for organizations to begin PQC migration planning now, covering NIST PQC standardization candidates (CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium), hybrid classical/PQC schemes, and inventory of crypto-agile dependencies.

talks.title: Alvaro Muñoz - SSO Wars: The Token Menace
talks.teaser: Catalogs critical vulnerability classes in SAML, OAuth, and JWT SSO implementations used across enterprise environments.
talks.summary:
SSO Wars: Attacking Single Sign-On

Alvaro Muñoz (Principal Security Researcher, GitHub Security Lab) presents a comprehensive attack taxonomy against enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO) implementations, demonstrating how identity federation protocols are systematically misimplemented.

SAML Vulnerabilities

The talk covers XML Signature Wrapping (XSW) attacks, where attackers inject a valid signature into an unsigned forged assertion without invalidating the cryptographic check. Muñoz demonstrates multiple XSW variants that bypass authentication in real-world SP implementations.

OAuth 2.0 and OIDC Attack Surface

Common OAuth misconfigurations including open redirectors, insufficient state parameter validation, and CSRF in authorization endpoints allow account takeover without any cryptographic break. The talk covers code injection via redirect_uri manipulation.

JWT Pitfalls

Muñoz documents the 'alg:none' attack, RSA/HMAC confusion attacks, and weak secret brute-forcing against JWT implementations, providing tooling and detection strategies.

talks.title: Alon Weinberg - Please Inject Me: A x64 Code Injection
talks.teaser: Introduces a novel x64 code injection technique that bypasses modern Windows security controls without process hollowing.
talks.summary:
Novel x64 Process Injection

Alon Weinberg presents a new code injection technique targeting 64-bit Windows that achieves code execution in arbitrary processes while evading common detection mechanisms.

Injection Without Hollowing

Unlike process hollowing (which unmaps the target executable's image), this technique injects shellcode into the target process's existing mapped sections using reflective loading, avoiding suspicious memory allocation patterns flagged by EDR solutions.

WoW64 and NTDLL Abuse

The technique leverages the WoW64 subsystem's heaven's gate mechanism and direct syscall stubs to bypass userland API hooks commonly deployed by AV/EDR to monitor API calls like VirtualAllocEx and WriteProcessMemory.

Detection and Mitigation

Weinberg provides behavioral detection signatures and discusses kernel-level controls (PatchGuard, Kernel Patch Protection) that could mitigate the technique.

talks.title: Ali Islam - Weaponizing Hypervisors to Beat Car and Medical Device Attacks
talks.teaser: Proposes using lightweight hypervisors as a security enforcement layer for automotive ECUs and implantable medical devices.
talks.summary:
Hypervisors as Embedded Security Controls

Ali Islam, security researcher at Cylera, presents research on deploying Type-1 hypervisors on resource-constrained embedded systems to enforce security policy on automotive ECUs and medical devices.

The Threat Model

Modern vehicles contain 100+ ECUs with no mandatory security boundaries; medical implants run legacy code on ARM Cortex-M devices. Both classes of devices present life-safety risk if compromised remotely.

Hypervisor Architecture for Constrained Systems

Islam demonstrates a modified ACRN-based hypervisor running on automotive-grade ARM Cortex-A processors, providing VM isolation between safety-critical and connected functions, with memory protection unit (MPU) enforcement.

Attack Prevention

By isolating the infotainment system (internet-connected) from the powertrain domain in separate VMs with restricted inter-VM channels, the hypervisor prevents lateral movement attacks observed in prior Jeep and Tesla research.

talks.title: Alexandre Borges - .NET Malware Threats: Internals And Reversing
talks.teaser: Deep-dives into .NET CLR internals to equip analysts with techniques for reversing obfuscated .NET malware families.
talks.summary:
.NET Malware Internals

Alexandre Borges, malware researcher, delivers an in-depth technical session on analyzing modern .NET-based malware, covering CLR internals, obfuscation techniques, and dynamic analysis strategies.

CLR Architecture Fundamentals

The talk begins with the Common Language Runtime's execution model — MSIL compilation, JIT compilation, AppDomain isolation, and the managed heap — providing the foundational context for understanding how malware abuses these mechanisms.

Obfuscation Techniques

Borges catalogs common .NET obfuscation strategies: string encryption, control flow flattening, method name mangling, and anti-decompilation tricks targeting dnSpy and ILSpy. He demonstrates automated de-obfuscation using de4dot and custom MSIL patching.

Dynamic Analysis with CLR Profiler

Using the CLR Profiling API, analysts can hook JIT compilation events to capture de-obfuscated MSIL at runtime without static unpacking. Borges demonstrates this against real AgentTesla and AsyncRAT samples.

talks.title: albinowax - HTTP Desync Attacks: Smashing into the Cell Next Door
talks.teaser: Presents HTTP request smuggling as a modern attack primitive for cache poisoning, session hijacking, and WAF bypass.
talks.summary:
HTTP Desync Attacks

James Kettle (albinowax), Director of Research at PortSwigger Web Security, presents HTTP request smuggling (desync attacks) — a rediscovered attack class with devastating impact on modern web infrastructure.

The Desync Primitive

HTTP/1.1 allows two mechanisms to delimit request bodies: Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding. When a frontend proxy and backend server disagree on which header takes precedence, an attacker can 'smuggle' a partial HTTP request that poisons the backend's request queue.

Attack Scenarios

Kettle demonstrates: bypassing WAFs and access controls by wrapping the prohibited request inside an innocuous smuggled prefix; hijacking other users' sessions by capturing their request data; and poisoning the shared reverse proxy cache to serve malicious responses to arbitrary users.

Real-World Impact

Findings affect major CDN providers and web frameworks. Kettle provides detection methodologies and recommends disabling HTTP/1.1 Keep-Alive on internal proxy-to-backend hops where possible.

talks.title: Brent Stone - Reverse Engineering 17+ Cars in Less than 10 Minutes
talks.teaser: Demonstrates automated CAN bus reverse engineering tooling that maps unknown message IDs to physical vehicle functions in minutes.
talks.summary:
Automated Automotive CAN Bus Reverse Engineering

Brent Stone presents a methodology and toolchain for rapidly reverse engineering CAN bus message formats across 17+ vehicle makes and models, reducing the time from plug-in to functional control mapping to under 10 minutes.

CAN Bus Fundamentals

CAN bus carries thousands of messages per second encoding sensor readings, control commands, and status telemetry from every ECU in the vehicle. Most automotive security research requires weeks of manual fuzzing to identify which message IDs control which functions.

Automated Discovery via Correlation

Stone's approach correlates CAN message timing and value changes with physical vehicle sensor readings (GPS speed, accelerometer, steering angle sensor from OBD-II) to automatically associate unknown message IDs with likely vehicle systems.

Cross-Vehicle Generalization

By building a database of correlated mappings across 17 vehicles, the tool identifies recurring message patterns (e.g., speed reporting formats) that generalize across manufacturers, accelerating subsequent vehicles.

talks.title: WillC - Phreaking Elevators
talks.teaser: Explores proprietary elevator controller protocols to unlock hidden floors, disable safety interlocks, and audit building security.
talks.summary:
Elevator System Hacking

WillC presents research into elevator control systems, exposing the security assumptions (or lack thereof) in building vertical transportation infrastructure used by millions daily.

Elevator Architecture

Modern elevators use proprietary serial protocols between the main controller, door controllers, and car operating panel. WillC reverse engineers these protocols from traffic analysis and physical inspection of controller PCBs.

Hidden Floor Access

Elevator service modes, activated through undocumented key sequences or injected serial commands, unlock floors not shown on the standard panel — fire service, machine room, and penthouse floors gated only by physical key switches with easily defeated logic.

Safety Interlocks and Remote Control

The talk demonstrates injecting commands to disable door-open safety circuits and send the car to arbitrary floors, and discusses the implications for building security, emergency evacuation, and physical penetration testing.

talks.title: Patrick Wardle - Harnessing Weapons of Mac Destruction
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how macOS malware authors abuse legitimate Apple APIs and signing to create persistent, undetected implants.
talks.summary:
macOS Offensive Tradecraft

Patrick Wardle (Principal Security Researcher, Jamf, founder of Objective-See) presents advanced macOS offensive techniques used by state-sponsored actors and commodity malware authors.

Code Signing and Notarization Bypass

Wardle demonstrates techniques to sign malicious payloads with developer certificates or abuse the ad-hoc signing mechanism, and discusses gaps in Apple's notarization service that allowed signed malware to pass automated scanning.

LaunchAgent and LaunchDaemon Persistence

Detailed coverage of macOS LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon persistence, including user-level and system-level plist injection, and how macOS System Integrity Protection (SIP) creates a false sense of security when attackers already have user-level code execution.

Keychain and iCloud Credential Theft

Wardle shows how malware with local privilege escalation can dump plaintext credentials from the macOS Keychain by abusing accessibility APIs and injection into trusted processes, bypassing keychain access prompts.

talks.title: Hadrian Barral - The ABC of Next Gen Shellcoding
talks.teaser: Introduces modern shellcoding techniques that survive ASLR, NX, and common AV detection by combining gadget chaining with runtime resolution.
talks.summary:
Modern Shellcoding Tradecraft

Hadrian Barral presents an updated shellcoding methodology that addresses the challenges introduced by modern exploit mitigations — ASLR, NX/DEP, stack canaries, and AV signature detection.

Position-Independent Shellcode

Classic shellcodes relied on fixed addresses. Barral demonstrates PIC techniques using delta stubs, hash-based API resolution, and EAT walking to locate and call Windows API functions without hardcoded addresses.

Gadget-Assisted Execution

For scenarios where classic shellcode is blocked by NX, Barral combines short-form ROP chains that pivot execution to a decoded shellcode stub, bypassing both DEP and common signature-based detections.

AV Evasion at the Shellcode Level

The talk covers junk code insertion, polymorphic encoding schemes, and sleep-before-decode techniques that defeat dynamic sandboxes with short analysis windows.

talks.title: Gregory Pickett - Breaking the Back End: Sometimes it's Just Bad Design
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how fundamental architectural design flaws in backend APIs create exploitable vulnerabilities no patch can fully address.
talks.summary:
Backend API Design Flaws

Gregory Pickett, founder of Hellfire Security, presents a series of real-world backend vulnerabilities stemming from architectural design failures rather than implementation bugs — flaws that persist even after individual CVEs are patched.

Insecure Direct Object References at Scale

Examples include healthcare and financial APIs that expose sequential integer identifiers for patient records and account numbers, enabling mass enumeration without authentication.

Broken Access Control Architectures

Pickett presents systems where authorization decisions are made client-side, with the backend trusting an unverifiable user role embedded in the JWT payload, enabling privilege escalation by token manipulation.

Business Logic Vulnerabilities

Beyond technical bugs, the talk covers business logic flaws — APIs that allow negative quantities in shopping carts, loyalty point transfers exceeding account balances, and time-of-check/time-of-use race conditions in financial transactions.

talks.title: Gerald Doussot - State of DNS Rebinding Attacks & Singularity of Origin
talks.teaser: Revives DNS rebinding as a practical attack against internal services and introduces the Singularity toolkit for automated exploitation.
talks.summary:
DNS Rebinding: Resurrected and Weaponized

Gerald Doussot presents updated DNS rebinding attack techniques and introduces Singularity of Origin, an open-source toolkit for automating DNS rebinding attacks against internal services.

The Attack Mechanism

DNS rebinding abuses the same-origin policy (SOP) by first pointing a domain at the attacker's server, delivering malicious JavaScript, then rapidly changing the DNS record to point at an internal IP. The victim's browser then sends XHR requests to the internal target, believing it's still on the attacker's origin.

Modern Browser Defenses and Bypasses

Browser vendors have attempted mitigations including DNS TTL pinning. Doussot demonstrates that many browsers still honor rebinding with TTLs as low as 0, and provides race-condition techniques to beat TTL-based protections.

Singularity Toolkit

The open-source Singularity tool automates the DNS server, payload delivery, and rebinding timing to attack routers, smart home devices, Kubernetes dashboards, and other internal web services exposed on RFC-1918 addresses.

talks.title: g richter - Reverse Engineering 4G Hotspots for Fun, Bugs, and Net Financial Loss
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers the firmware of commercial 4G hotspot devices to find authentication bypasses and persistent backdoor injection points.
talks.summary:
4G Hotspot Firmware Reversing

g richter presents research into popular commercial 4G mobile hotspot devices used by millions for personal and enterprise connectivity.

Firmware Extraction

Using UART serial ports exposed on the PCB and JTAG probing, the researcher extracts full firmware images from multiple hotspot models including devices from major US carriers.

Vulnerability Discovery

Static analysis of extracted firmware reveals hardcoded administrative credentials, unauthenticated web management interfaces accessible from the LTE network, and command injection vulnerabilities in the device management daemon.

LTE Network-Side Attacks

Beyond local attacks, the talk examines the AT command interface exposed over USB and vulnerabilities in the device's PPP and DHCP implementations that could be exploited by a malicious carrier network.

talks.title: finalphoenix - Rise of the Hypebots: Scripting Streetwear
talks.teaser: Exposes the underground economy of sneaker bots, showing how scripted buyers defeat retailer anti-bot measures at scale.
talks.summary:
The Sneaker Bot Ecosystem

finalphoenix presents an in-depth look at the technical and economic ecosystem of sneaker and streetwear bots — automated purchasing tools that dominate limited-release drops.

Bot Architecture

Modern sneaker bots use headless browsers (Puppeteer, Playwright), residential proxy pools, CAPTCHA-solving services, and webhook-based coordination to purchase limited inventory faster than humans can respond.

Anti-Bot Arms Race

Retailers deploy fingerprinting (browser behavior analytics, mouse movement ML models), queue systems, and challenge pages. finalphoenix demonstrates how bot operators defeat each measure through browser spoofing, human-like interaction simulation, and early access account farming.

Market Economics

The talk quantifies the financial scale: popular sneaker drops sell out in under 5 seconds, with bot operators reselling inventory for 2–10× retail, generating thousands of dollars per release day.

talks.title: Eyal Itkin - Say Cheese: How I Ransomwared Your DSLR Camera
talks.teaser: Exploits the Picture Transfer Protocol over USB and Wi-Fi to remotely ransomware a Canon DSLR camera.
talks.summary:
Ransomwaring a DSLR Camera

Eyal Itkin (vulnerability researcher, Check Point Research) demonstrates a complete exploit chain targeting Canon DSLR cameras, achieving remote code execution over both USB and Wi-Fi using the Picture Transfer Protocol (PTP).

Picture Transfer Protocol Attack Surface

PTP is an unauthenticated protocol designed for image transfer. Itkin identifies multiple buffer overflow and integer overflow vulnerabilities in the Canon EOS 80D firmware's PTP request handler, exploitable over both USB and the camera's built-in Wi-Fi.

Full RCE and Ransomware Payload

After triggering RCE, the researcher writes a proof-of-concept ransomware that encrypts all photos on the SD card using AES and displays a ransom demand on the camera's LCD, demonstrating the real-world impact of ignoring IoT security.

Coordinated Disclosure

Canon was notified before the talk and released firmware updates. Itkin discusses the disclosure timeline and the broader implications for embedded device update mechanisms.

talks.title: Elliott Thompson - MI CASA SU CASA: My 192.168.1.1 is Your 192.168.1.1
talks.teaser: Shows how attacker-controlled web pages can pivot through DNS rebinding to attack consumer routers and LAN-connected devices.
talks.summary:
LAN Pivoting via Browser

Elliott Thompson presents research on attacking home and small office networks from an external attacker's web page, using the victim's browser as a network pivot.

DNS Rebinding Chained with Router Exploits

Using DNS rebinding to satisfy the same-origin policy, Thompson's exploit code executes requests against the victim's router management interface (typically 192.168.1.1), exploiting known authentication bypass CVEs in popular consumer routers.

Beyond Routers: LAN Device Discovery

After gaining router access, the attacker can query the router's DHCP lease table to enumerate all connected devices and pivot to attack printers, NAS devices, and smart home hubs on the victim's LAN — all from a malicious web page.

Real-World Scope

Thompson demonstrates the attack against several top-selling router models and provides a browser-based scanning tool that enumerates common RFC-1918 ranges without requiring any local software installation.

talks.title: Elie Bursztein - Deep Learning: Revolutionizing Side Channel Cryptanalysis
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how deep learning models outperform classical DPA attacks for power-analysis-based key extraction from AES implementations.
talks.summary:
Deep Learning for Side Channel Attacks

Elie Bursztein (Lead Security Researcher, Google) presents research applying deep neural networks to power side-channel analysis, achieving superior key extraction performance compared to classical Differential Power Analysis (DPA).

Classical vs. ML-Based SCA

Classical DPA requires profiling attacks with a known device or relies on univariate statistical models. Neural network models trained on power traces directly learn the mapping from trace shape to intermediate computation values, handling misalignment and noise that breaks classical methods.

Convolutional Neural Network Architecture

Bursztein's approach uses CNNs to process raw power traces, with the model learning alignment-invariant features automatically. On STM32 AES implementations, the CNN recovers full 128-bit AES keys with fewer traces than classical CPA.

Open-Source Dataset and Framework

The talk releases a public power trace dataset and open-source framework for training and evaluating SCA models, enabling reproducible research.

talks.title: droogie - Go NULL Yourself
talks.teaser: Revives Windows null session attacks against modern Active Directory environments, demonstrating significant unauthenticated enumeration capabilities.
talks.summary:
NULL Sessions in Modern Active Directory

droogie presents research demonstrating that null session (unauthenticated) SMB enumeration — a technique from the Windows NT era — remains surprisingly effective against modern Windows Server and Active Directory environments due to default configuration weaknesses.

Null Session Enumeration

Null sessions allow unauthenticated SMB connections that can enumerate domain users, groups, shares, and group policy information through MSRPC endpoints (SAMR, LSARPC) without any valid credential.

Default Configuration Analysis

Despite Microsoft's attempts to restrict null sessions over the years, many organizations leave legacy settings enabled, and some configurations required for backward compatibility (pre-Windows 2000 compatibility mode) restore enumeration capabilities.

Attack Chaining

The talk demonstrates how unauthenticated user enumeration chains into password spraying, AS-REP roasting (Kerberos pre-authentication disabled accounts), and targeted phishing using harvested employee names.

talks.title: Dr Bramwell Brizendine - JOP ROCKET: A Wicked Tool for JOP Gadget Discovery
talks.teaser: Introduces JOP ROCKET, an open-source tool for discovering Jump-Oriented Programming gadgets to build control-flow hijacking exploits.
talks.summary:
JOP Gadget Discovery with JOP ROCKET

Dr Bramwell Brizendine presents JOP ROCKET (Jump-Oriented Programming Rapid Open Catalog of Key Execution Targets), an open-source tool for automating the discovery of JOP gadgets in binary executables.

JOP vs. ROP

Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) chains gadgets ending in RET instructions; Jump-Oriented Programming (JOP) instead chains gadgets ending in indirect JMP or CALL instructions, enabling exploitation even when the stack is controlled by a shadow stack or CET enforcement.

JOP ROCKET Architecture

The tool supports x86, x86-64, and ARM architectures, implements multiple search strategies (linear sweep, recursive descent), and classifies discovered gadgets by type (dispatcher gadgets, functional gadgets, update gadgets) according to the formal JOP gadget taxonomy.

Real-World Exploit Construction

Brizendine demonstrates constructing a JOP chain against a real CVE in a consumer application, showing the full workflow from binary analysis through gadget selection to exploit delivery.

talks.title: Douglas McKee - HVACking: Understand the Delta Between Security and Reality
talks.teaser: Exposes critical authentication and authorization failures in enterprise HVAC and building automation systems reachable from corporate networks.
talks.summary:
HVAC Security Failures

Douglas McKee (Lead Vulnerability Researcher, McAfee ATR) presents findings from a systematic assessment of enterprise HVAC and building automation systems (BAS), revealing severe security gaps that allow attackers to manipulate physical infrastructure.

BACnet and Modbus Exposure

Building automation protocols (BACnet, Modbus, LonWorks) were designed without authentication or encryption. McKee demonstrates scanning for internet-exposed BACnet/IP devices and enumerating available control points (temperature setpoints, damper positions, alarm states) with no credentials required.

Corporate Network Lateral Movement

In typical enterprise environments, HVAC controllers share network segments with IT infrastructure. McKee demonstrates pivoting from a compromised workstation to the BAS network and remotely controlling CRAC units in data centers — potentially causing thermal damage or triggering fire suppression systems.

Vendor Response

The talk covers disclosure efforts with major BAS vendors and the difficulty of patching legacy embedded controllers deployed in multi-decade building infrastructure.

talks.title: Dirk-jan Mollema - I'm in Your Cloud: Pwning Your Azure Environment
talks.teaser: Demonstrates a complete Azure Active Directory attack chain from initial access through Global Administrator privilege escalation.
talks.summary:
Azure AD Attack Chain

Dirk-jan Mollema (security researcher, Fox-IT) presents a comprehensive attack chain against Microsoft Azure environments, starting from a compromised employee workstation and escalating to full Azure tenant compromise.

Pass-the-Hash to Azure AD

From a domain-joined Windows machine, the attacker extracts NTLM hashes and uses them against Azure AD's legacy authentication endpoints (Basic Auth, NTLM over WinRM), bypassing modern MFA policies that don't apply to legacy protocols.

AADConnect Exploitation

Mollema reveals that Azure AD Connect sync accounts (required for hybrid identity) hold excessive privileges. Extracting the sync account credentials from the AADConnect server's encrypted configuration allows on-premises-to-cloud lateral movement with Directory Synchronization account rights.

Global Admin Privilege Escalation

Chaining these techniques, the attacker escalates from a standard user to Global Administrator in the Azure tenant, achieving full control over all Azure subscriptions, O365, and Intune-managed devices.

talks.title: Dimitry Snezhkov - Zombie Ant Farm: Practical Tips for Playing Hide and Seek
talks.teaser: Presents advanced C2 communication obfuscation techniques that blend malicious traffic into legitimate business protocols.
talks.summary:
Covert C2 Channel Techniques

Dimitry Snezhkov (Senior Red Team Operator, Optiv) presents practical techniques for establishing and maintaining covert command-and-control channels that evade network detection and traffic analysis.

Protocol-Level Obfuscation

Rather than encrypting traffic (which produces anomalous TLS patterns), the talk demonstrates tunneling C2 communications inside legitimate application protocols: HTTP over standard ports with realistic User-Agent strings and cookie formats, DNS TXT record-based channels, and Microsoft Graph API-based C2 using SharePoint and OneDrive as intermediaries.

Beacon Pattern Randomization

Deterministic beacon patterns (every N seconds) are trivially detected. Snezhkov presents jitter algorithms and sleep skew techniques that randomize beacon timing to match observed human workflow patterns.

Network Sensor Evasion

The talk covers techniques to evade JA3/JA3S TLS fingerprinting, byte-frequency analysis, and deep packet inspection by configuring C2 frameworks (Cobalt Strike, Covenant) to mimic legitimate application profiles.

talks.title: Daniel Crowley - Key Search Attacks Against Modern Symmetric Ciphers
talks.teaser: Revisits meet-in-the-middle and other key search attacks against symmetric ciphers, examining their relevance to modern key length choices.
talks.summary:
Key Search Attacks on Symmetric Ciphers

Daniel Crowley (Research Director, IBM X-Force Red) presents a comprehensive examination of key search attacks targeting symmetric block ciphers, assessing their practical viability against current key lengths.

Meet-in-the-Middle Attacks

The classical meet-in-the-middle attack against 2DES reduces the effective key space from 2^112 to 2^56 with a time-memory tradeoff. Crowley examines modern variants that extend this to triple-key constructions and analyze whether similar weaknesses apply to AES key scheduling.

Distributed Key Search Infrastructure

Using cloud GPU instances (AWS p3 instances with V100s), Crowley demonstrates cost-effective key search against weak key lengths, quantifying the cost to brute-force 56-bit and 64-bit keys in current dollars.

Key Length Recommendations

The talk concludes with practical guidance on minimum key lengths for symmetric ciphers given current and projected hardware capabilities, providing 10-, 20-, and 30-year threat horizons.

talks.title: Daniel Romero - Why You Should Fear Your Mundane Office Equipment
talks.teaser: Demonstrates persistent backdoors and network pivots achievable through common office equipment including printers, scanners, and VOIP phones.
talks.summary:
Office Equipment as Attack Infrastructure

Daniel Romero presents research on security vulnerabilities in mundane office equipment — printers, multifunction devices, IP phones, and network-attached scanners — showing how attackers use these devices as persistent staging points.

Printer Exploitation

Enterprise laser printers from major vendors run full embedded Linux with web management interfaces. Romero demonstrates unauthenticated remote code execution in HP, Xerox, and Lexmark management portals, providing persistent access that survives endpoint security agent deployment.

Print Job Interception

Beyond code execution, printers that spool jobs locally allow attackers to intercept, copy, and exfiltrate sensitive printed documents including M&A communications, HR records, and legal filings.

Network Pivoting Through IoT

Office IoT devices (HVAC controllers, badge readers, digital signage) run stripped-down embedded Linux with minimal security and provide network footholds on VLANs that corporate workstations cannot directly access.

talks.title: Damien Cauquil - Defeating Bluetooth Low Energy 5 PRNG for Fun and Jamming
talks.teaser: Breaks the BLE 5.0 channel hopping PRNG to predict future advertisement channels and enable targeted jamming of Bluetooth 5 devices.
talks.summary:
BLE 5 PRNG Attack

Damien Cauquil (security researcher, Digital Security) presents a cryptanalytic attack against the Bluetooth Low Energy 5.0 pseudo-random number generator used for channel hopping in advertisement and connection events.

BLE Channel Hopping Mechanism

BLE uses FHSS across 37 advertising channels and 37 data channels, with channel selection determined by a PRNG seeded from the access address and connection parameters. The PRNG is documented in the Bluetooth Core Spec as a linear feedback shift register.

PRNG Prediction and Targeted Jamming

By observing a small number of advertisement packets, Cauquil recovers the PRNG state and predicts future channel selections. Using a software-defined radio, he then jams only the predicted channels, creating selective denial-of-service against specific BLE devices while leaving other nearby devices unaffected.

Impact on BLE 5 Long Range

The attack extends to BLE 5's Long Range (coded PHY) mode, which extends range to ~1km but uses the same vulnerable PRNG, enabling targeted jamming of medical implants and industrial sensors at significant distance.

talks.title: Christopher Wade - Tag Side Attacks Against NFC
talks.teaser: Demonstrates NFC tag-side attacks that manipulate reader-side applications via malformed tag responses and relay injection.
talks.summary:
NFC Tag-Side Security

Christopher Wade presents research on the underexplored attack surface of NFC from the tag's perspective — malicious or manipulated tags that attack the reader-side software stack.

Malformed Tag Responses

NFC reader software (on smartphones, POS terminals, access control readers) must parse complex tag response PDUs. Wade demonstrates buffer overflows, integer overflows, and use-after-free vulnerabilities in reader software triggered by carefully crafted malformed NDEF records.

Relay Attacks via Proxy Tags

Using a custom NFC relay tool, Wade shows how a malicious tag can transparently proxy reader queries to a remote legitimate tag, enabling long-range NFC relay attacks against transport payment cards and building access badges.

Android and iOS Parsing Vulnerabilities

The talk includes specific CVEs in Android's NFC stack and iOS's Core NFC framework triggered by specially crafted NFC tag data, demonstrating impact on mainstream mobile devices.

talks.title: Christopher Roberts - Firmware Slap: Automating Discovery of Exploitable Vulnerabilities in Firmware
talks.teaser: Presents Firmware Slap, a framework combining concolic execution and fuzzing to automatically discover exploitable bugs in embedded firmware.
talks.summary:
Automated Firmware Vulnerability Discovery

Christopher Roberts presents Firmware Slap, an open-source framework for automated vulnerability discovery in embedded device firmware.

Framework Architecture

Firmware Slap combines three analysis phases: static binary analysis using Angr for taint tracking, concolic execution to explore complex conditional branches, and targeted fuzzing guided by the static analysis results to generate exploiting test cases.

Firmware Extraction and Normalization

The framework handles the heterogeneous input formats (raw binary blobs, UBIFS/SquashFS filesystem images, encrypted firmware) produced by different vendors' firmware update mechanisms, automating extraction and binary identification.

Real-World Results

Firmware Slap identified multiple previously undiscovered vulnerabilities in consumer router firmware from D-Link and TP-Link, including stack buffer overflows in HTTP server CGI handlers, within minutes of automated analysis.

talks.title: Campbell Murray - GSM: We Can Hear Everyone Now
talks.teaser: Demonstrates practical GSM interception using commodity SDR hardware and open-source software to decrypt 2G voice calls.
talks.summary:
Practical GSM Voice Interception

Campbell Murray (Global Head of Security Services, BlackBerry) presents a practical demonstration of GSM (2G) voice call interception using commodity software-defined radio hardware and open-source software tools.

GSM Security Model Failures

GSM provides one-way authentication (network authenticates subscriber; subscriber cannot authenticate network) and uses the A5/1 stream cipher, which was broken cryptanalytically in 2009 with rainbow table attacks. GSM networks also transmit calls in cleartext when the network operator sets the encryption indicator to none.

Full Interception Setup

Using a $35 RTL-SDR dongle, Osmocom software, and publicly available A5/1 rainbow tables, Murray demonstrates decrypting and recording live 2G voice calls within range of a passive SDR antenna — no IMSI catcher required for unencrypted calls.

LTE Fallback Vulnerabilities

The talk covers LTE networks' forced fallback to 2G (SRVCC) as an attack vector: a malicious cell tower can force a target's LTE phone to downgrade to vulnerable 2G for interception.

talks.title: Bruce Schneier - Information Security in the Public Interest
talks.teaser: Bruce Schneier argues that security technologists have a moral obligation to engage with policy and serve the public interest, not just clients.
talks.summary:
Security as a Public Good

Bruce Schneier, cryptographer, security technologist, and fellow at the Harvard Kennedy School Belfer Center, delivers a keynote arguing that information security professionals must move beyond client service to engage with the broader societal implications of their work.

The Public Interest Problem

Schneier argues that security traditionally serves the interests of those who pay for it — corporations and governments — often at the expense of individuals, minorities, and the public. Mass surveillance infrastructure built for intelligence agencies gets repurposed for authoritarian oppression. Security features designed to protect corporate IP surveil employees.

Security Professionals as Policy Actors

The talk calls on hackers and security researchers to engage with lawmakers, regulators, and civil society organizations to shape technology policy in ways that protect civil liberties and democratic institutions. Schneier cites examples of researcher testimony contributing to GDPR provisions and surveillance reform legislation.

Actionable Pathways

Schneier outlines specific ways security professionals can contribute: expert witness testimony, pro bono work for civil society organizations (EFF, ACLU), participation in standards bodies, and public education campaigns to raise awareness of surveillance risks.

talks.title: Brad Dixon - Cheating in eSports: How to Cheat at Virtual Cycling
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers the Zwift virtual cycling platform to demonstrate trivial speed cheating via client-side protocol manipulation.
talks.summary:
Cheating in Virtual Cycling: Zwift

Brad Dixon presents a technical analysis of cheating in Zwift, the popular indoor cycling eSports platform used by professional athletes and millions of recreational cyclists.

Zwift Architecture and Trust Model

Zwift relies on a Windows/macOS client application that reads power meter and speed sensor data via Bluetooth/ANT+ and transmits it to cloud servers. The server trusts client-reported power values with minimal server-side validation.

Protocol Reverse Engineering

Dixon reverse engineers the Zwift client's network protocol using Wireshark and custom parsers, identifying the UDP and WebSocket messages that transmit rider power, cadence, and position.

Cheat Implementation

By injecting modified packets reporting artificially high power output, a rider can ride at simulated speeds of hundreds of kilometers per hour. Dixon demonstrates this in a live race, winning by minutes with near-zero physical effort — exposing the fundamental trust problem in all competitive online fitness applications.

talks.title: Bill Swearingen - HAKC THE POLICE
talks.teaser: Exposes persistent plaintext transmission failures in P25 public safety radio networks used by law enforcement and first responders.
talks.summary:
P25 Public Safety Radio Vulnerabilities

Bill Swearingen (Security Consultant, ICSDefense) revisits and extends prior research on Project 25 (P25) digital radio networks used by US law enforcement, federal agencies, and first responders, demonstrating that years-old interception vulnerabilities persist.

P25 Encryption Failures

P25 radios support encryption (DES-OFB, AES) but deployment is inconsistent. Many agencies transmit plaintext by default, allowing passive monitoring with commodity RTL-SDR hardware and open-source P25 decoders (OP25, DSDPlus).

Encryption Status Indicator Bypass

Even when encryption is intended, officers can accidentally transmit in the clear if the encryption indicator is disabled by misconfiguration or radio malfunction. Swearingen documents cases of sensitive operational communications intercepted in cleartext during active law enforcement operations.

Strike Attack on Encrypted P25

Using an IMSI-catcher-like approach adapted for P25, Swearingen demonstrates a downgrade attack that causes encrypted radios to fall back to analog, enabling passive interception of sensitive tactical communications.

talks.title: Bill Graydon - Duplicating Restricted Mechanical Keys
talks.teaser: Demonstrates that restricted key systems — marketed as uncopyable — can be precisely duplicated using 3D printing and inexpensive blank grinding.
talks.summary:
Breaking Restricted Key Systems

Bill Graydon presents research demonstrating that restricted mechanical key systems — keys marketed as 'uncopyable' due to patent restrictions on key blanks — can be defeated using accessible technology.

How Restricted Key Systems Work

Restricted key systems (Medeco, Mul-T-Lock, Abloy Protec) use proprietary key blank profiles available only to licensed dealers and require mandatory dealer verification before cutting. The business model relies on blank scarcity rather than cryptographic security.

3D Printing Key Blanks

Using open-source 3D printing files for documented restricted key profiles, Graydon creates functional PLA and resin key blanks that fit restricted cylinders. While early prints lacked the tensile strength for heavy padlocks, modern SLS-printed nylon blanks operate comparably to metal blanks for light-duty cylinders.

Photogrammetric Key Cloning

By briefly photographing a restricted key against a known-measurement reference background, the exact cut depths can be measured photogrammetrically and replicated on a key cutting machine, bypassing the need for a restricted blank entirely.

talks.title: Bill Demirkapi - Are Your Child's Records at Risk? The Current State of School Security
talks.teaser: A high school student discovers unauthenticated API endpoints exposing millions of K-12 student records from major edtech platforms.
talks.summary:
Edtech API Security Failures

Bill Demirkapi, a high school student at the time of research, presents critical vulnerabilities discovered in two major K-12 educational technology platforms serving millions of students.

Revel Systems: Unauthenticated Student Data Access

The Revel Systems parent portal API exposes student schedules, grades, teacher information, and disciplinary records for all students at connected schools through unauthenticated REST endpoints — accessible by simply incrementing student IDs.

PowerSchool: SQL Injection in SIS

PowerSchool, the dominant student information system in US K-12 schools, contains SQL injection vulnerabilities in authenticated endpoints that allow any school employee with login credentials to extract the full district database, including PII for students, parents, and staff.

Ethical Disclosure Journey

Demirkapi walks through his disclosure experience as a minor, including vendor non-responses, legal threats, and eventually coordinating disclosure through the school district, providing a candid account of responsible disclosure challenges.

talks.title: Bernhard Mueller - The Ether Wars: Exploits, Counter-Exploits, and Honeypots
talks.teaser: Analyzes the adversarial ecosystem of Ethereum smart contract exploits and counter-exploits, including honeypot contracts designed to trap attackers.
talks.summary:
Ethereum Smart Contract Adversarial Ecosystem

Bernhard Mueller (Trail of Bits security engineer) presents research on the predatory dynamics of the Ethereum smart contract ecosystem — a battleground where exploiters, counter-exploiters, and honeypot operators compete for funds.

Common Smart Contract Vulnerabilities

The talk reviews the canonical exploit classes: reentrancy (as exploited in the DAO hack), integer overflow/underflow, front-running via transaction ordering, and access control failures in proxy patterns.

Honeypot Contract Analysis

The Ethereum blockchain contains thousands of honeypot contracts — deliberately vulnerable-looking contracts designed to trap inexperienced attackers who attempt to exploit them, only to discover a hidden mechanism that transfers their deposited funds to the honeypot creator.

Counter-Exploit Bots

Mueller analyzes sophisticated automated bots that monitor the Ethereum mempool for transactions exploiting vulnerable contracts and front-run them with higher gas prices to steal the attacker's extracted funds, creating a recursive exploit ecosystem.

talks.title: Ben Sadeghipour - Owning The Clout Through Server Side Request Forgery
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how SSRF vulnerabilities provide a direct path from web application to cloud metadata service, IAM credentials, and full account compromise.
talks.summary:
SSRF to Cloud Account Takeover

Ben Sadeghipour (NahamSec, prolific bug bounty hunter and security educator) presents a practical methodology for chaining Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities into full cloud account compromise.

SSRF Mechanics and Discovery

The talk covers techniques for identifying SSRF parameters — URL-fetching features, webhook configurations, image proxy endpoints, PDF generation services — and demonstrates bypassing common blacklist-based SSRF filters using IP encoding, DNS rebinding, and IPv6.

Cloud Metadata Service Exploitation

By directing SSRF requests to 169.254.169.254 (AWS EC2 metadata service) or equivalent Azure/GCP endpoints, attackers retrieve IAM role credentials for the compromised application server, obtaining cloud API access keys with the application's assigned permissions.

Privilege Escalation to Account Takeover

With IAM credentials, attackers enumerate accessible resources (S3 buckets, RDS snapshots, Secrets Manager entries), demonstrating how a single SSRF bug in a low-privilege service leads to full cloud account compromise through privilege escalation via IAM policy misconfigurations.

talks.title: Ariel Herbert-Voss - Don't Red Team AI Like a Chump
talks.teaser: Provides a structured adversarial ML red team methodology for attacking production AI systems beyond naive input perturbation.
talks.summary:
Red Teaming AI Systems

Ariel Herbert-Voss (OpenAI safety researcher) presents a structured methodology for red teaming AI and machine learning systems, going beyond naive adversarial examples to address production attack surfaces.

Beyond Adversarial Images

The popular conception of ML red teaming focuses on adversarial perturbations (image classifiers fooled by small pixel changes). Herbert-Voss argues this misses the most impactful attack surfaces in production systems: training data poisoning, model extraction, and API-level inference attacks.

Model Extraction and Intellectual Property Theft

By sending carefully crafted queries to a black-box ML API, attackers can reconstruct an approximate clone of the target model. The talk demonstrates extracting a functionally equivalent model from a commercial API with a budget of under $100 in API calls.

Production Deployment Attacks

The talk covers supply chain attacks on ML pipelines: poisoning training datasets via malicious contributions to public datasets, inserting backdoors into pre-trained models distributed via model hubs, and exploiting serialization vulnerabilities (pickle deserialization) in model file formats.

talks.title: Anish Athalye - Want Strong Isolation? Just Reset Your Processor
talks.teaser: Proposes processor reset as an isolation primitive to provide stronger guarantees than cache flush-based mitigation of microarchitectural side channels.
talks.summary:
Processor Reset as an Isolation Primitive

Anish Athalye (PhD student, MIT CSAIL) presents IORR (Isolation via Processor Reset), a research proposal for achieving strong security isolation in shared-processor environments by resetting processor microarchitectural state between security domains.

Microarchitectural Side Channel Background

Spectre and Meltdown revealed that shared microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictors, TLBs) leaks information between isolation domains in shared systems. Software mitigations (KPTI, Retpoline) impose significant performance overhead and remain incomplete.

Reset as a Clean Slate

The IORR architecture partitions execution into epochs, performing a lightweight processor reset (microarchitectural state flush without a full power cycle) when switching between security domains. This provides cryptographic-quality isolation guarantees equivalent to running on separate physical processors.

Performance Analysis

Athalye presents empirical performance measurements of IORR on RISC-V prototype hardware, demonstrating that hardware-assisted epoch switching adds only microseconds of overhead — comparable to OS context switch costs — while providing stronger isolation than current software mitigations.

talks.title: Andy Grant - Unpacking PKGs: A Look Inside macOS Installer Packages
talks.teaser: Dissects macOS PKG installer internals to reveal how malware authors abuse the package format for persistence and privilege escalation.
talks.summary:
macOS PKG Package Abuse

Andy Grant (Security Research Engineer, NCC Group) presents a deep technical analysis of the macOS PKG installer format and how malware authors abuse it for code execution, persistence, and privilege escalation.

PKG Format Internals

The macOS PKG format (an XAR archive containing a Bill of Materials, component archives, and pre/post-flight scripts) provides attackers with multiple code execution hooks: preinstall and postinstall scripts run with root privileges during installation and are commonly exploited by malware bundled with pirated software.

Code Signing and Notarization Gaps

Grant demonstrates that signing a malicious PKG with a valid Apple Developer certificate satisfies macOS Gatekeeper checks. Until 2019, malicious PKGs with valid developer signatures bypassed notarization review, enabling macOS malware distribution through official channels.

Forensic Analysis and Detection

The talk provides forensic analysis techniques for identifying malicious PKG installers — inspecting pre/postinstall scripts, embedded binary payloads, and anomalous LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon installations triggered by installer scripts.

talks.title: Orange Tsai - Infiltrating Corporate Intranet Like NSA: Pre-auth RCE on Leading SSL VPNs
talks.teaser: Discovers critical pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerabilities in three leading enterprise SSL VPN products.
talks.summary:
SSL VPN Pre-Auth RCE Research

Orange Tsai (Principal Security Researcher, DEVCORE) presents critical vulnerabilities in three leading enterprise SSL VPN products that allow unauthenticated remote code execution — providing direct access to corporate intranets without credentials.

Pulse Secure VPN

CVE-2019-11510: An unauthenticated arbitrary file read in Pulse Secure VPN allows reading cached plaintext credentials from active VPN sessions, providing credential-based access. CVE-2019-11539: Remote code execution via unauthenticated format string injection in the ping diagnostic function.

Fortigate SSL VPN

CVE-2018-13379: Unauthenticated path traversal allows downloading arbitrary files from the Fortigate VPN appliance, including session files containing cleartext VPN credentials and authentication tokens.

Palo Alto GlobalProtect

CVE-2019-1579: Format string vulnerability in the GlobalProtect portal pre-auth request handler allows unauthenticated remote code execution on the VPN gateway.

Mass Exploitation Impact

All three CVEs were actively exploited in the wild within weeks of disclosure by nation-state actors (APT5, suspected Chinese-nexus) to gain persistent access to government and critical infrastructure networks.

talks.title: Olivier Bilodeau - Industry of Social Media Manipulation Driven by Malware
talks.teaser: Exposes the malware-driven underground industry providing fake engagement (followers, likes, shares) powering disinformation operations at scale.
talks.summary:
Malware-Backed Social Media Manipulation

Olivier Bilodeau (Cybersecurity Research Director, GoSecure) presents research exposing the technical infrastructure behind coordinated social media manipulation operations powered by malware botnets.

The Manipulation Industry

A well-organized underground market provides 'social media marketing' services: fake followers, likes, retweets, YouTube views, and review scores. These services are typically powered by infected devices in consumer malware botnets, not server farms, providing realistic geographically distributed traffic.

Malware Integration

Bilodeau analyzes malware families that include social media manipulation modules alongside traditional banking trojans and ransomware droppers, showing how click fraud, credential theft, and fake engagement generation run as parallel monetization threads on the same compromised systems.

Operation Analysis

The talk includes analysis of a specific manipulation operation's infrastructure: C2 panels managing 100,000+ infected devices performing coordinated social media actions, complete with task scheduling, anti-detection delays, and revenue reporting dashboards.

talks.title: Nina Kollars - Confessions of an Nespresso Money Mule
talks.teaser: A delightful true story of accidentally discovering and exploiting a significant logic flaw in Nespresso's coffee capsule loyalty program.
talks.summary:
The Accidental Coffee Fraud

Nina Kollars (security researcher and professor, Naval War College) delivers a hilarious and insightful true story about accidentally discovering and exploiting a business logic vulnerability in Nespresso's coffee capsule loyalty program.

The Discovery

While making a legitimate purchase, Kollars discovers that Nespresso's reward point system contains a logic flaw: returning capsules generates points independent of the original purchase transaction, enabling unlimited point generation through a cycle of purchase, return, and repeat.

Escalating the Exploit

What begins as a casual observation becomes a systematic investigation, with Kollars documenting the full scope of the vulnerability, the economics of the exploit (maximum point generation rate vs. time invested), and the logistical challenges of laundering coffee capsules.

Security Lessons

Beyond the entertainment value, the talk provides a serious analysis of business logic flaw discovery methodology, the ethics of exploiting vendor vulnerabilities for personal gain, and how loyalty program fraud scales into multi-million dollar criminal enterprises.

talks.title: Nikhil Mittal - RACE: Minimal Rights and ACE for Active Directory Dominance
talks.teaser: Introduces RACE, an open-source toolset for persistent Active Directory access using minimal-privilege ACL modifications invisible to most monitoring.
talks.summary:
Active Directory ACL Abuse with RACE

Nikhil Mittal (founder of Hacking Articles and nishang) presents RACE (Registry ACLs for Covert Access Extension), a toolset for maintaining persistent Active Directory access through stealthy ACL modifications that require only minimal privileges.

ACL-Based Persistence

Rather than using traditional high-privilege persistence mechanisms (domain admin group membership, Golden Tickets) that trigger alerting, RACE exploits the Active Directory ACL model to grant targeted, minimal permissions that enable re-access when needed without maintaining constant high-privilege presence.

Registry ACL Modifications

The technique modifies Windows registry key ACLs and Active Directory object attribute ACLs to allow low-privilege accounts to read DPAPI-protected secrets, modify user account properties, or reset passwords — actions that appear as routine system operations in event logs.

Minimal Footprint Operations

Mittal demonstrates the complete RACE attack chain from initial domain user compromise to persistent administrative access using only ACL modifications, avoiding account changes and group additions that trigger modern detection rules.

talks.title: Nicolas Oberli - Poking the S in SD Cards
talks.teaser: Explores the attack surface of the SD card specification, revealing undocumented commands and firmware update mechanisms that enable persistent device compromise.
talks.summary:
SD Card Security Research

Nicolas Oberli (Hardware Security Researcher, Kudelski Security) presents research into the security properties of the SD card specification, exposing an underexplored attack surface in the most ubiquitous storage medium.

SD Card Architecture

SD cards contain a complete embedded system: an 8051 or ARM microcontroller, flash memory chips, and proprietary firmware that implements wear leveling, error correction, and the SD protocol state machine. The controller firmware is the primary attack target.

Undocumented Vendor Commands

Oberli discovers that all major SD card manufacturers implement proprietary extensions to the SD command set, accessible via specific multi-byte command sequences. These vendor commands include firmware update triggers, raw flash access modes, and diagnostic functions undocumented in public specifications.

Firmware Update Persistence

Exploiting the firmware update mechanism, Oberli demonstrates implanting custom code in SD card firmware that intercepts specific file reads/writes — enabling a malicious SD card to exfiltrate data to a hidden partition or trigger malware execution when inserted into a target device.

talks.title: Mike Spicer - I Know What U Did Last Summer: 3 Years of Wireless Monitoring at DEF CON
talks.teaser: Presents three years of wireless traffic analysis from DEF CON, revealing attendee device behavior, probe requests, and passive surveillance capabilities.
talks.summary:
Three Years of Passive Wireless Monitoring at DEF CON

Mike Spicer presents longitudinal research from three consecutive DEF CON conferences where he deployed a mobile passive 802.11 monitoring rig, collecting and analyzing wireless traffic patterns from conference attendees.

Passive Monitoring Setup

The monitoring rig — built into a backpack — uses multiple high-gain antennas and commodity 802.11 cards in monitor mode across all Wi-Fi channels, logging probe requests, management frames, and broadcast traffic without association to any network.

Device Fingerprinting via Probe Requests

Even without connecting to any network, smartphones constantly broadcast probe requests containing the SSIDs of previously connected networks. Spicer demonstrates how these probes reveal attendees' home and work networks, travel history, and device model information through the MAC address OUI.

Year-over-Year Behavioral Trends

Tracking probe request patterns across three DEF CON conferences reveals trends in device security posture (MAC address randomization adoption, probe request frequency reductions) and demonstrates the persistent effectiveness of passive wireless surveillance despite industry countermeasures.

talks.title: Michael Stepankin - Apache Solr Injection
talks.teaser: Discovers Solr injection, a new web attack class targeting Apache Solr search parameters to achieve SSRF and remote code execution.
talks.summary:
Apache Solr Injection Attacks

Michael Stepankin presents Solr Injection, a new class of web application vulnerability analogous to SQL injection but targeting Apache Solr search infrastructure.

Solr Attack Surface

Apache Solr powers search functionality in many enterprise applications. When user input is incorporated directly into Solr query parameters, attackers can inject additional parameters that modify query behavior, similar to second-order SQL injection.

SSRF via RequestDispatcher

Solr's RequestDispatcher parameter (shards) accepts URLs for distributed search across Solr shards. By injecting a shards parameter, attackers redirect Solr to make arbitrary HTTP requests to internal services — a server-side request forgery vector that bypasses application-level SSRF mitigations.

RCE via Velocity Template Injection

Solr's velocity response writer interprets Velocity template syntax in query parameters. Injecting Velocity template expressions achieves server-side template injection leading to arbitrary Java code execution on the Solr server, as demonstrated against real enterprise deployments.

talks.title: Michael Leibowitz - EDR is Coming: Hide Yo Sh!t
talks.teaser: Catalogs practical techniques for evading modern EDR solutions across file system, memory, process, and network visibility layers.
talks.summary:
EDR Evasion Techniques

Michael Leibowitz (Senior Security Researcher, Nvidia) presents a comprehensive survey of techniques for evading modern Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions, covering all visibility layers from file system to network.

EDR Architecture and Visibility

Modern EDRs instrument systems through kernel minifilter drivers (file I/O), ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) providers, AMSI hooks, userland API hooks via IAT/inline patching, and network kernel callbacks. Effective evasion requires understanding and defeating each layer.

File System Evasion

Alternate Data Streams (ADS), process hollowing without disk-based staging, and reflective DLL loading avoid triggering file-based signatures. Timestomping and VSS manipulation defeat forensic artifact recovery.

Memory and Process Evasion

Direct system calls (bypassing userland hooks), Heaven's Gate (WoW64 transitions), and process doppelgänging abuse Windows transactional NTFS to create process images that exist only in transaction memory, evading both file scanning and memory scanning.

Network Evasion

Using legitimate cloud services (OneDrive, Slack, GitHub) as C2 channels, and domain fronting through major CDNs, prevents network-based EDR from distinguishing malicious from legitimate traffic.

talks.title: Matt Wixey - Sound Effects: Exploring Acoustic Cyberweapons
talks.teaser: Demonstrates malware that weaponizes speakers, headphones, and industrial ultrasonic emitters to cause physical harm, data exfiltration, and device damage.
talks.summary:
Acoustic Cyberweapons

Matt Wixey (Security Researcher, PwC) presents research into weaponizing audio hardware — speakers, headphones, piezoelectric transducers, and industrial ultrasonic emitters — through malware, achieving physical harm and covert data exfiltration.

Speaker Damage via Resonance

Wixey demonstrates malware that drives consumer speakers and headphones with resonant frequencies and excessive amplitude, causing permanent physical damage to speaker cones and hearing damage at close range — a denial-of-service attack with physical consequences.

Ultrasonic Data Exfiltration

Using inaudible ultrasonic frequencies (20kHz+), the research demonstrates covert data exfiltration from air-gapped systems via ultrasonic acoustic channels between speaker and microphone-equipped devices at distances up to several meters.

Industrial Ultrasonic Manipulation

Industrial ultrasonic cleaning and welding systems use high-power transducers (hundreds of watts). Wixey demonstrates that software control of these systems enables weaponized ultrasonic beams capable of causing physical injury at short range.

talks.title: Marina Simakov - Relaying Credentials has Never Been Easier
talks.teaser: Presents new NTLM relay attack techniques targeting previously protected services in modern Windows environments.
talks.summary:
Modern NTLM Relay Attacks

Marina Simakov (security researcher, Preempt Security) presents new NTLM relay attack vectors and techniques that bypass Microsoft's published mitigations and target services previously believed to be protected from relay attacks.

NTLM Relay Background

NTLM relay attacks intercept NTLM authentication handshakes and forward them to a different target server, authenticating as the victim to services they didn't intend to access. Microsoft's mitigations (SMB signing, EPA/channel binding) block relay in many scenarios.

Bypass Techniques

Simakov presents CVE-2019-1040, a vulnerability in the NTLM authentication protocol that allows dropping MIC (Message Integrity Code) and modifying authentication messages, enabling relay even to SMB-signed targets. The bypass breaks EPA (Extended Protection for Authentication) for many real-world configurations.

Cross-Protocol Relay

The talk demonstrates relaying NTLM from HTTP to LDAP/LDAPS, enabling creation of new computer accounts and delegation rights in Active Directory without any credentials — providing a path to full domain compromise from only network access.

talks.title: Maksim Shudrak - How To Improve Coverage-Guided Fuzzing & Find New 0days
talks.teaser: Presents advanced AFL fuzzing strategies including custom mutators, target-aware input seeds, and sanitizer integration to maximize 0day discovery.
talks.summary:
Advanced Coverage-Guided Fuzzing

Maksim Shudrak (Security Researcher) presents techniques to improve the effectiveness of AFL-based coverage-guided fuzzing for discovering previously unknown vulnerabilities.

Limitations of Vanilla AFL

Standard AFL fuzzing saturates coverage quickly on most targets, spending 95%+ of compute cycles generating inputs that exercise already-covered paths. Without targeted feedback, the fuzzer fails to reach deep vulnerability sites.

Custom Mutator Strategies

Shudrak presents grammar-aware mutators for structured input formats (XML, JSON, binary protocols) that generate semantically valid inputs reaching deeper code paths than random byte flipping. He demonstrates integrating libFuzzer's dictionary and structure-aware mutation into AFL campaigns.

Sanitizer Integration and Triage

Running fuzzing targets compiled with AddressSanitizer (ASan), UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (UBSan), and MemorySanitizer dramatically increases crash detection coverage. Shudrak presents automated crash deduplication and exploitability triage workflows using tools like ASAN crash analyzer and Exploitable.

talks.title: Leon Jacobs - Meticulously Modern Mobile Manipulations
talks.teaser: Presents a systematic methodology for intercepting and manipulating traffic from modern mobile applications that implement certificate pinning and root detection.
talks.summary:
Modern Mobile App Interception

Leon Jacobs presents practical techniques for intercepting and manipulating network traffic from modern Android and iOS applications that implement multiple layers of anti-analysis protections.

Certificate Pinning Bypass

The talk covers bypassing certificate pinning using Frida dynamic instrumentation, hooking the platform SSL libraries at the function level to override pinning checks. For apps with multiple pinning layers (HTTPS, WebSocket, gRPC), Jacobs demonstrates a systematic bypass methodology.

Root/Jailbreak Detection Bypass

Root and jailbreak detection checks using file system probes, package manager queries, and native code integrity checks are bypassed using Magisk Hide (Android) and Liberty Lite (iOS), with Frida hooks handling any remaining programmatic checks.

Deep Traffic Analysis

With interception established, the talk demonstrates modifying API responses in transit, replaying authenticated requests with modified parameters, and extracting API keys and session tokens from intercepted traffic.

talks.title: Kyle Gwinnup - Next Generation Process Emulation with Binee
talks.teaser: Introduces Binee, an open-source Windows process emulator designed for rapid malware analysis without requiring a full Windows environment.
talks.summary:
Windows Process Emulation with Binee

Kyle Gwinnup (Principal Software Engineer, Crowdstrike) presents Binee, an open-source Windows PE binary emulator built on the Unicorn CPU emulator and a custom Windows API stub library.

Emulation vs. Sandboxing

Traditional malware sandboxes run samples in real Windows VMs, requiring significant infrastructure and risking VM escape. Binee emulates the Windows execution environment at the API level — the CPU executes real code, but Windows API calls are handled by Binee's stub implementations rather than a real Windows kernel.

API Stub Library

Binee implements hundreds of Windows API functions (file I/O, registry, network, process management) as Python stubs that log API calls and return realistic values, enabling analysis of malware's intended behavior without requiring a full Windows environment.

Analysis Use Cases

Binee rapidly executes and logs API call sequences from packed and obfuscated malware, providing high-confidence behavioral indicators without sandbox evasion. The talk demonstrates unpacking and analyzing AgentTesla, Emotet, and custom-packed implants.

talks.title: Katherine Pratt - Hacking Your Thoughts: Batman Forever meets Black Mirror
talks.teaser: Explores security and privacy vulnerabilities in consumer EEG brain-computer interfaces used for meditation, gaming, and attention measurement.
talks.summary:
Brain-Computer Interface Security

Katherine Pratt presents security and privacy research on consumer brain-computer interface (BCI) devices — EEG headsets marketed for meditation guidance, attention training, gaming, and neurofeedback therapy.

Consumer EEG Device Ecosystem

Devices such as the Emotiv EPOC+, Muse headband, and Neurosky MindWave use consumer-grade dry EEG electrodes to capture brainwave signals transmitted via Bluetooth to companion applications. Pratt reverse engineers the BLE communication protocols and data formats.

Brainwave Data Privacy

EEG signals contain more information than device manufacturers disclose: raw brainwave data can reveal emotional states, cognitive load, attention levels, and in some cases medical conditions (epilepsy markers, ADHD patterns). Pratt analyzes the data privacy policies of commercial BCI platforms.

Attack Scenarios

The talk demonstrates eavesdropping on BLE brainwave data transmissions, manipulating neurofeedback training sessions by injecting false signals, and conducting covert cognitive load measurements using compromised BCI devices to infer user activity and mental state.

talks.title: Junyu Zhou - Web2Own: Attacking Desktop Apps from Web Security's Perspective
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how web security vulnerabilities (XSS, SSRF, path traversal) in Electron desktop applications escalate to full OS code execution.
talks.summary:
Attacking Electron Desktop Applications

Junyu Zhou presents a systematic methodology for attacking Electron-based desktop applications using web security techniques, demonstrating that web vulnerabilities in desktop contexts result in full OS-level code execution.

Electron Architecture

Electron applications bundle Chromium and Node.js, creating a hybrid web/desktop environment. The main process has full Node.js capabilities (file system, shell, network); renderer processes run web content in a sandbox. The critical boundary is the IPC bridge between renderer and main.

XSS to RCE

In Electron apps that disable contextIsolation or enable nodeIntegration in renderer processes, stored XSS in rendered content executes arbitrary JavaScript with full Node.js capabilities — providing immediate file system access, shell command execution, and credential extraction from the local system.

Real-World Targets

Zhou demonstrates successful exploitation of XSS vulnerabilities in Slack (before fixes), VS Code extensions, and several popular productivity applications, achieving code execution through seemingly low-severity web vulnerabilities.

talks.title: Joseph Cox - How You Can Buy AT&T, T-Mobile, and Sprint Real-Time Location Data
talks.teaser: Exposes the underground market for US carrier real-time location data, demonstrating purchase of precise GPS location for any phone number.
talks.summary:
Carrier Location Data Market

Joseph Cox (journalist, Motherboard/VICE) presents investigative findings on the commercial market for US carrier real-time location data, demonstrating that any person's precise real-time GPS location can be purchased for approximately $300.

Location Data Supply Chain

US carriers (AT&T, T-Mobile, Sprint, Verizon) sell aggregated location data to 'location aggregators' (Zumigo, LocationSmart, Babel Street) for legitimate uses (fraud detection, roadside assistance). These aggregators resell access to hundreds of downstream 'location intelligence' companies.

High-Risk Access Points

Bail bond companies and private investigators access location data through specialized 'skip tracing' services that provide real-time phone location without a court order. Cox demonstrates purchasing the real-time location of a specific person's phone with consent, revealing precise coordinates accurate to within 100 meters.

Policy Response

Following Cox's reporting (published in Motherboard), all four major US carriers announced they would cease selling location data to aggregators. The FCC ultimately issued $200M+ in fines for unauthorized location data sharing.

talks.title: Jmaxxz - Your Car is My Car
talks.teaser: Reveals how telematics API vulnerabilities allowed unauthorized remote unlocking, location tracking, and engine start of any vehicle in a major connected car fleet.
talks.summary:
Connected Car Telematics Exploitation

Jmaxxz presents research disclosing critical vulnerabilities in a major connected car telematics platform that allowed unauthorized remote control and tracking of vehicles across an entire fleet.

Connected Car Architecture

Modern connected vehicles include a telematics control unit (TCU) that maintains a persistent cellular connection to the manufacturer's cloud platform, enabling remote lock/unlock, geofencing alerts, remote engine start, and location tracking through a smartphone app.

API Authentication Bypass

Reverse engineering the companion mobile application reveals the telematics API structure. Jmaxxz discovers that the API uses a predictable vehicle identifier (VIN-derived) as the primary authorization token, allowing enumeration and impersonation of any vehicle in the fleet.

Unauthorized Remote Control

With the authorization token, any registered account holder can remotely unlock, locate, and start any vehicle in the fleet — not just vehicles they own. The talk demonstrates unlocking a vehicle belonging to a consenting third party from miles away, then tracking its real-time location.

talks.title: Jiska - Vacuum Cleaning Security: Pinky and The Brain Edition
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers robot vacuum cleaners to reveal camera surveillance capabilities, Bluetooth vulnerabilities, and cloud data exposure.
talks.summary:
Robot Vacuum Security Research

Jiska Classen (security researcher, Technical University of Darmstadt) presents comprehensive security research on consumer robot vacuum cleaners, revealing surveillance capabilities and vulnerabilities in popular models.

Firmware Analysis

Using UART debugging interfaces and firmware extraction from NAND flash, Classen analyzes the embedded Linux firmware in Roomba, Neato, and iRobot models. The firmware includes cloud connectivity modules, camera subsystems, and navigation AI components.

Camera and LiDAR Privacy

Camera-equipped models (iRobot Roomba i7, Ecovacs) capture and upload environmental imagery to cloud servers for navigation and customer support. Classen analyzes what imagery is retained, for how long, and who can access it — raising significant home privacy concerns.

Bluetooth Protocol Vulnerabilities

The Bluetooth LE control protocol used by vacuum cleaners contains authentication weaknesses that allow unauthorized device control from within Bluetooth range — enabling an attacker to disable the vacuum, alter its schedule, or dump its internal map of the home's floor plan.

talks.title: Jesse Michael - Get Off the Kernel if You Can't Drive
talks.teaser: Demonstrates persistent firmware-level implants that survive OS reinstalls by exploiting UEFI driver loading and Secure Boot bypass vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
UEFI and Firmware Persistence
